suspects.claim: Ties between listed strikes go to the first in list order, not to the one nearer spot +/- 1.50: with 583 unlisted and spot 581.90 it picks 582 (1.40 away) over 584 (0.60 away).
Candidates run $5 either side of the target, so when the strikes just above spot are unlisted it can buy an in-the-money call.
Ctrl+C while it waits for IB's commission reports leaves a closed trade out of the CSV.
Port 7496 might be let through without --live.
Port 4002 might be treated as a live port.
With no USD row it might size from the BASE-currency row instead of stopping.
Started late, it might take a later bar as the opening range.
A price exactly at a trigger might count as a breakout.
Sizing might still return one contract the balance cannot cover.
A missing commission might be filled in from the fee estimate.
A wait might use time.sleep, which stops ib_async's event loop.
ib_async's [None] for an unknown contract is a truthy list and might pass for success.
UTC bar dates might fail to match the New York 9:30 open.
The breaker might trip one loss late.
Delayed prices (data type 3) might be traded on.
After a trade it might take a new signal while SPY is still past the trigger.
